title: license show
description: What <app> license show answers with -o json, on envelope/v2, for licenses of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 (license-payload.schema.json): the app's license state and whether it warns, whether this build is a release, its active license, its trial, and every feature in its feature state with where it is unlocked from, so the CLI, its JSON, the top bar's badge and the License group on the app's Settings page show the same answer and none of them works anything out (ADR-L3, L8, L9). Every license the app can see, and the files it refused, are license list's (license-list.schema.json); one license by its id is license show <id>'s (license.schema.json). mankit's license check makes it for every app, so every app answers it alike. mankit/v2's LicenseShow is the answer before it.

data.description: The app's license state and warn, its build, its active license, its trial, the counts and its features.

state.description: What the badge and the License group say, one word for the license state of the whole app (ADR-L3), worked out here once; whether the build is a release is build's alone to say. The first of these that holds decides it. licensed: the active license has not ended, has begun and, when it names lines, names this build's line (ADR-L10, V-10). trial: the trial runs (trial, ADR-L9). free: anything else, so use is free (ADR-L3): no active license, or one not begun yet, ended, broken or not naming this build's line, and no trial, or one ended. The app never takes another license by itself when the active one does not run (ADR-L8).

endedOn.description: The active license's last day, when state is free and that license has ended, so ADR-L3's notice names the day and a page never picks a license. Absent otherwise.

sentence.description: The one sentence a reader shows for the app's license state, made by mankit's license check and shown word for word: readers never build or change it, so the CLI, the web badge and panel and the TUI say the same. Present when the state has one: a running trial, with its days left and last day; an ended trial; licensed, naming whom the active license is for; and an active license that has ended or is broken, saying why the app runs on its trial or free (ADR-L8). Absent otherwise. Its words are the license check's to choose.

warn.description: True when a reader shows the license state in its warn colour; the answer decides and readers never do (ADR-L3). True when state is licensed and the active license is in the warning ADR-L3's built-in threshold license-expiring sets; when state is trial and the trial is in its last days, as that threshold counts them; and when state is free and the trial or the active license has ended, until it is replaced or removed (ADR-L3). Absent or false otherwise, so a license that never ends never warns.

active.description: The app's active license, the one its features and state rest on (ADR-L8), as license list's row gives it. Present while one is active, even when it has ended or does not name this build's line, as the app never switches to another license by itself. Absent when none is active: there is no license, or the chosen file was refused, and sentence then says why.

features.description: Every feature of the app, in the order its feature list gives them: its feature state and where it is unlocked from, so the License group draws this answer alone (ADR-L2, L8).

allOf.description: A day a license ended is named only while use is free, and it always warns.
Licensed means an active license is given and has not ended.
A trial state means the trial is listed and has not ended.
A running trial means the state is trial, never free.
A day a license ended names the active license, which has ended.

trial.description: The app's trial, a rule in mankit and not a license: every enterprise feature of the app for ADR-L9's trial length from its first start, for the product line stamped in its build, with nothing signed (ADR-L9). When it started is the trial note's to say (trial-started.schema.json). Absent when the app has no trial, as on its first start it held a license and wrote no note.

until.description: The trial's last day: the note's day plus ADR-L9's trial length, less one, as the first day counts, so a reader shows when it ends.

daysLeft.description: The days left until the trial's last day, 0 once it has ended. license check gives only this; when to warn is the threshold's to say (ADR-L3).

ended.description: True once the trial's last day has passed: the features it opened are locked again, and what they made stays readable (ADR-L3).

allOf.description: An ended trial has no days left.

feature.description: One feature of the app: its feature state, each field as mankit/v1 defs' featureState says, and where it is unlocked from, a row of the License group's features table (ADR-L8).

from.description: Where the feature is unlocked from, worked out with state (ADR-L8, L9). license: the active license runs and names it; trial: the active license does not run or does not name it, and the trial runs; none: nothing opens it, as a free feature needs nothing and an enterprise feature with none is locked.

until.description: The last day the feature stays open, an RFC 3339 date: the last day of what unlocks it, the active license's until or the trial's until. Absent when from is none, and when an active license that never ends opens it.

allOf.description: featureState's own rules hold here too.
A feature nothing opens has no last day.
A feature a trial opens stays open until the trial ends.
A license names enterprise features only, and a trial opens only those, so a free feature is never unlocked from one (ADR-L2, L9).

day.description: A day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC: the one form every day in this answer takes.
